editorial_article:
"4," frequently referred to by fans as "Grass," is a haunting and ethereal composition from Aphex Twin's seminal 1994 studio album, *Selected Ambient Works Volume II*. Released on Warp Records, this collection marked a significant departure from the more dance-oriented ambient techno of the producer's debut, *Selected Ambient Works 85–92*. Instead, *Volume II* moved into purely experimental, drone-heavy, and minimalist territory, deeply informed by Richard D. James's interest in lucid dreaming and abstract, non-linear soundscapes.

Like most of the tracks on the album, "4" was originally released without a formal title, represented instead by an abstract circular icon in the liner notes that corresponded to the track's sonic profile—in this case, a soft, pastoral shape. The track itself is a quintessential example of the "chilly," sparse, and evocative aesthetic that defines the record. It avoids the traditional rhythmic structures of his earlier work, favoring a sustained, slightly melancholic atmosphere that resonates with a sense of isolation and internal reflection. It is frequently cited as one of the standout, more accessible moments of the record, capturing the unique, otherworldly mood that solidified Aphex Twin's legacy as a pioneer of experimental electronic and ambient music. Retrospective critics continue to view *Volume II* as a monumental work in the genre, and "4" remains a key touchstone in the evolution of the ambient sound.
